turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you holding up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got a coding interview with a whiteboard round next week and I panic when someone watches me write code.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's really common. The best trick is talking out loud as you go, so they're following your thinking, not just watching.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Even when I don't know the answer yet?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Especially then. Say what you're considering, why you'd rule something out. Interviewers often care more about that than the perfect solution.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And if I get totally stuck?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Say so, and try a simpler version of the problem first. It shows you can break things down.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I practise on paper or

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Paper's fine, but practise without a computer and with a friend or a timer. The pressure is what you're training for.
